title: Public-domain evidence audit for real calibration domains, missing slots, and outcome-blind nonresponse follow-up
adjudicands: Count candidates satisfying every empirical-separator field at score 1.
Count candidates satisfying every single-domain calibration-support field at score 1.
Count candidates satisfying every missingness-alignment field at score 1.
Count public survey candidates satisfying every outcome-blind validation field at score 1.
Compute signed, absolute, mean, RMS, and maximum residuals for the five NIST X4 melt-pool-camera calibration pairs.
Construct a conservative common-input graph without converting unknown independence into independent domains.

hypotheses.claim: At least one reviewed public candidate is sufficient for a real empirical separator certificate.
hypotheses.prediction: At least one candidate scores 1 on all nine required fields.
hypotheses.reject: No candidate scores 1 on all nine fields.

hypotheses.claim: The NIST AMMT releases provide real single-domain calibration evidence even if they do not establish independent domains.
hypotheses.prediction: At least one candidate has public identity-indexed raw values, calibration lineage, and stable public bytes, and the five X4 calibration residuals are exactly reproducible.
hypotheses.reject: No candidate qualifies or an independent implementation disagrees on any residual statistic.

hypotheses.claim: An expected command trigger plus an unlocated statement that frames were dropped is equivalent to an authenticated null-slot ledger.
hypotheses.reject: The reviewed release documents loss but does not bind every absent frame to an authenticated expected slot.

hypotheses.claim: The NSFG public release permits outcome-blind validation-subsample narrowing without restricted records.
hypotheses.prediction: The public candidate scores 1 on every outcome-blind validation field.
hypotheses.reject: Selection is temporally blind but sampled-case paradata, selection flags, or missing outcomes required for the bound are not public.

hypotheses.claim: Raw channels, instruments, laboratories, or signed reports can be used as the denominator of independent-domain resilience when shared inputs are only partly documented.
hypotheses.prediction: Every observed channel can be assigned its own evidenced calibration and common-cause domain.
hypotheses.reject: Any candidate contains shared or unknown standards, clocks, specimens, processors, control streams, preparation, or selection mechanisms that prevent that assignment.

decisionRules.promoteEmpiricalSeparator: Only if H1 is supported and the qualifying candidate has a pre-fixed blind partition and an independent reference.
decisionRules.promoteCalibrationSupport: Only as evidence for the named single measurement chain; never as cross-domain independence or process accuracy.
decisionRules.promoteMissingnessAudit: Only if every expected event has a stable identity and every absent observation remains as an explicit null with reason and epoch.
decisionRules.promoteNonresponseNarrowing: Only if public records expose the outcome-blind subsample probabilities, selected and unselected rosters, later outcomes, and target-variable denominator.
decisionRules.stop: Stop and issue a set-valued or design-only verdict if any required field is partial, restricted, inferred from file absence, or reused as its own independent reference.

minimumDecisiveTests: Programmatic field-by-field qualification of all six candidates under four frozen rules.
Independent recomputation of the five NIST calibration residuals from manifest values.
Ablation showing that treating each partial field as complete changes qualification and is therefore not allowed.
Conservative domain graph for NIST X16 and NSFG that labels unknown edges rather than assuming independence.
safety: The cycle uses public metadata and aggregate survey documentation only. It does not process respondent-level restricted data, identify people, operate machinery, or infer production safety from benchmark calibration residuals.
